anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly : Bottleneck in generation, flushing, archival or retention of write-ahead log records, stalling commit processing and write throughput.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : On-disk data or index pages have become corrupted or internally inconsistent, making persisted structures logically or physically unreliable.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Client-to-server transport, listener or connection-handling resources are saturated or unstable, delaying or aborting session establishment and data transfer.

When these three root causes strike simultaneously, the database may exhibit a multi-layered failure signature: commits hang or time-out, yet even successful transactions later surface missing or duplicated rows due to latent corruption; error logs show alternating bursts of log-flush and log-sync waits, page-checksum failures and connection-refused messages; clients experience a mix of slow authentication, dropped sessions, and data-integrity exceptions. Recovery utilities and background check-pointers run continuously but fall behind because log archival stalls, while network retransmissions and half-open sockets amplify commit latency. Administrative attempts to rebuild indexes or run integrity checks are throttled by both log I/O saturation and unreliable network channels, making the true extent of corruption hard to assess.

Causal chain: network congestion and listener saturation increase round-trip latency for commit handshakes and archiver file transfers, lengthening the time each transaction occupies the log buffer. The swollen log backlog forces aggressive checkpointing and log switches; if the underlying data pages are already corrupt, these checkpoints repeatedly hit verification errors, provoking partial rollbacks and even more redo generation, further overloading the log subsystem. Conversely, corruption in indexes or data blocks can trigger excessive redo (e.g., repetitive page-clean operations or index rebuild attempts) that drives the log system into saturation. The resulting log-flush stalls prolong transaction hold-times, thereby keeping sockets open longer and inflating the population of active connections, which worsens the existing network bottleneck. This self-reinforcing loop degrades both durability and consistency guarantees, making OLTP workloads unable to meet latency or correctness SLAs while obscuring the primary point of failure.

entry.official_description: Failed to establish an internal server connection to execute plugin operations since the server does not have available connections, please increase @@GLOBAL.MAX_CONNECTIONS. Server error: %i.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with connection establishment, authentication exchange, protocol correctness, network reachability, or client/server communication stability.
entry.solution_guidance: Check endpoint reachability, authentication flow, connection limits, protocol compatibility, transport stability, and client connection lifecycle management.
